chapter_name: Sangya Ke Vikari Tatva: Ling, Vachan, Aur Karak (Noun Modifiers: Gender, Number, and Case)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will learn the magical elements that change the shape of nouns—Gender, Number, and the invisible connectors called Cases!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Nouns are 'Vikari' (changeable) words. They don't stay the same forever! Depending on if they are male or female (Ling), one or many (Vachan), or how they connect to the action (Karak), their spelling and form will change. Like 'लड़का' (Boy) changing to 'लड़के' (Boys).

In Hindi, it is not just living things that are male or female; even non-living things have a gender! For example, a Table (मेज़) is feminine (Striling), but a Bed (पलंग) is masculine (Pulling). The trick to finding the gender of an object is to use it in a sentence with a verb or adjective!

Vachan tells us if a noun is Ek (One) or Anek (Many). 'Ekvachan' is singular (किताब - Book), and 'Bahuvachan' is plural (किताबें - Books). Keep an eye on the dot (Bindi)! Sometimes changing to plural requires adding a nasal dot, like लड़की -> लड़कियाँ.

Karak (Case) acts like glue, connecting nouns to the verb in a sentence. Without Karak, words would just float around meaninglessly. For example, 'राम रावण मारा' makes no sense. Add Karak signs: 'राम ने रावण को मारा' (Ram killed Ravan). Now it makes perfect sense!

There are 8 types of Karak, and each has its own special symbol (Vibhakti). Memorize this chant: 'Karta NE, Karm KO, Karan SE, Sampradan KE LIYE, Apadan SE (separation), Sambandh KA/KE/KI, Adhikaran MEIN/PAR, Sambodhan HEY/AREY!'.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The 'Gender Detective' Test
fun_activity.instructions: Pick 5 non-living objects in your room (like Fan, Door, Window, Pen, Book). Create a simple Hindi sentence for each to find out its gender. Example: 'पंखा चल रहा है' (Fan is running - Pulling). 'हवा चल रही है' (Wind is blowing - Striling).

quick_recap: ⭐ Nouns change their form based on Ling (Gender), Vachan (Number), and Karak (Case).
⭐ Hindi has only two genders: Pulling (Masculine) and Striling (Feminine). Even objects have genders.
⭐ Vachan has two types: Ekvachan (Singular) and Bahuvachan (Plural).
⭐ Karak shows the relationship of a noun/pronoun with the verb using symbols like 'ne', 'ko', 'se'.
⭐ There are 8 types of Karaks in Hindi Grammar.
